column2: Know that it is as if there were a person afflicted by the misery of cold—only a warm fire, or the light of the sun, or garments and the like can give him respite, so that he can find comfort; or one afflicted by the misery of heat, whose only respite is glades, springs, and so on; or one travelling a long road, whose only respite is cool shade; or one afflicted by thirst, whose only respite is pure, cold water; or one afflicted by hunger, whose only respite is ample, fine viands; or one afflicted by illness, whose only respiteis skilled physicians and nurses; or one afflicted by fear, whose only respite is a staunch companion.

column1: 若渴所逼唯清冷水； 若飢所逼唯多美膳， 若病所逼惟良醫藥及供侍者； 若怖所逼惟強伴侶。 如是， 大王！
column2: “Just so, O great king!

column1: 一切眾生死箭所中， 無復勢力、無復救護、無所歸依、無所投竄，
column2: all beings, when they are struck by the arrow of birth-and-death, no longer have any strength, no longer have any protection, no longer have anything to depend upon, no longer have anywhere to flee.

column1: 臨欲捨命解支節時， 血肉枯竭心胸熱惱， 焦渴所逼張口太息， 手足紛亂無所堪能，
column2: On the verge of leaving this life, the limbs and members fall apart, and flesh and blood becomes arid and parched, and the heart is tormented by fever, and a parching thirst oppresses you, and the mouth gapes, and you breathe in great gasps, and your arms and legs flail chaotically; you can do nothing and have no strength, .

column1: 廣說乃至彼於爾時唯有正法， 能為救護、能為宮室、能作歸依， 是所奔趣是所投竄，
column2: . . and so on, down to: . . . At that time, righteous Dharma is all there is that can serve as salvation, or can serve as a palace, or can function as a refuge, or is a direction to run, or is a place to flee to, or can pluck beings out of the woe of birth-and-death.

column1: 能拔眾生出生死苦。 所以者何？
column2: And why is that?

column1: 「大王當知！
column2: “O great king!

column1: 如是身者， 雖加守護雖久洗飾， 雖以眾多上妙飲食恣意飽滿， 及至臨終， 要當不免飢渴所逼而便捨命。
column2: Know that the body being thus, one might well lavish protection upon it; one might well for a long time wash it and adorn it; one might well sate it as much as one pleases with exquisite food and drink—but when one reaches the brink of the end of life, there is no way one will avoid dying oppressed by hunger and thirst.

column1: 「大王當知！
column2: “O great king!

column1: 如是身者， 雖常澡浴， 塗香末香熏香花鬘隨意嚴飾， 由此自體穢漏成故， 臨捨命時， 終必歸於不淨臭穢。
column2: Know that the body being thus, one might well bathe it always, and festoon it as one likes with scented unguents, or perfumed talcs, or sweet perfumes, or garlands—but because it is essentially made of filth and corruption, when one stands on the verge of giving life up, it will finally and certainly return to foulness, stench and filth.

column1: 「大王當知！
column2: “O great king!

column1: 如是身者， 雖以種種上妙衣服覆蔽纏裹， 由此自身諸不淨物所合成故， 於命終時， 要當不淨種種流出。
column2: Know that the body being thus, one might well swaddle it and wrap it and cover it with all sorts of exquisite garments—but because it is innately a compound of impure things, when life is at an end, it will surely ooze with all sorts of corruption.

column1: 「大王當知！
column2: “O great king!

column1: 如是身者， 雖處宮室后妃婇女內官美人眷屬圍遶， 作眾伎樂種種倡伎， 以自娛樂歡喜快樂， 臨命終時，
column2: Know that the body being thus, one might well dwell in a palace, surrounded by an entourage of queens, concubines, courtesans, and beauties, and have them perform dance and music and all sorts of entertainments in order to amuse oneself, cheer oneself, and enjoy oneself—but when the end of life is nigh, ill omens will spontaneously appear, and you will surely be terrified, woebegone, and sorely troubled.

column1: 自見惡相， 要當驚怖憂悲苦惱。 「大王當知！
column2: “O great king!

column1: 如是身者， 雖處宮室綵飾圖畫殿閣樓臺， 戶牖軒窓重關密掩， 種種香花以自嚴飾， 種種燈燭增光照明， 施設珍奇屏障帷幄， 燒眾名香散諸妙花， 香花寶瓶處處陳列， 安置種種金銀琉璃眾寶床座， 敷設上妙氍氀錦繡文蓐花氈，
column2: Know that the body being thus, for all that one might dwell in a palace, with tapestries and paintings, pavilions and turrets, doors and shutters and verandas and windows, ensconced in layered walls and closely secluded; with all kinds of flowers to adorn oneself, and all kinds of lamps to brighten and lighten up the place; appointed with expensive and exquisite screens and canopies; burning renowned incenses, and scattering wonderful flowers, with fragrant blossoms in precious vases lined up everywhere in rows; setting out all kinds of couches and divans of gold, silver, and beryl, and laying out the finest felt mats, and brocade, and patterned rugs, and floral felts; with vermilion cushions placed at both ends of the couches, covered with the finest embroidered kerchiefs and fancy coverlets, so that waking or sleeping, in rest or repose, one is blissful and absorbed—but once life is over, you will perceive none of that.

column1: 床座兩頭俱置丹枕， 覆以上妙綺帊錦衾， 寤寐安寢歡娛耽著， 於命終後無所覺知， 或送屍骸置於葬所， 烏鵲鵰鷲狐狼野干， 餓狗鵄梟諸惡禽獸爭共食噉， 骨肉膿血鬚髮糞穢， 流溢地上臭處可惡。
column2: “And perhaps they will send your corpse to be flung on the charnel ground, and crows and carrion birds, and foxes, wolves, and jackals, and ravenous dogs and owls, and all manner of evil birds and beasts will contend with one another to eat your bones, flesh, marrow and blood, and your whiskers and hair and excrement and ordure will spill across the ground, in an abominable place of stench.

column1: 「大王當知！
column2: “O great king!

column1: 如是身者， 先常乘馭香象駿馬眾寶輦輿， 擊鼓吹貝作大音樂， 眾寶傘蓋隨侍於後， 執持扇拂掩映搖動， 無量勇健象軍馬軍車軍步軍導從前後，
column2: Know that the body being thus, where formerly, you always rode perfumed elephants, or fine steeds, or bejewelled palanquins; with kettledrums beating and conches blasting, and a great fanfare struck up; followed behind by attendants shading you from the sun with jewelled canopies and flourishing yak-tail fly-whisks; with countless doughty and valiant regiments of elephant, horse, chariots and infantry, parading before and behind and guarding your left and right; with hundreds and thousands of ministers and courtiers sincerely singing your praises, and the people of the cities and towns saluting and cheering— although you might have enjoyed such excellent rewards as these, and power and glory, before long, you will certainly close your eyes, and stretch out your arms, and stir no more; your corpse will lie flat on its back on the funeral bier, and be carried by a throng out the gate of the city; and your parents, wives, children, brothers, sisters, menials, servants, courtiers, attendants, relatives and intimates will follow behind and on either side, their hearts trammelled by grief, their hair loose and unbound, raising their hands to bludgeon their heads, beating their breasts and dolefully keening, so shaken by grief they collapse, all wailing, ‘Woe!’ And the people of the cities and towns of the land, seeing them, will cry out a lament, and accompany the corpse to the funeral ground.

column1: 防衛左右百千臣僚竭誠敬奉， 城邑士庶合掌驚歎。 雖受如是勝妙果報自在榮華， 不久要當瞑目辟手無復動搖， 橫屍偃仰喪車輿上， 眾人荷挽出大城門， 父母妻子兄弟姊妹作使僮僕群僚輔佐， 親屬內人隨從左右， 心纏憂惱頭髮被散， 舉手拍頭椎胸悲噎， 哀感崩慟皆言： 『苦哉！ 』城邑國人覩之號慕。 隨送葬所， 或有露屍施諸禽獸， 鳥鵲餓狗鵰鷲鵄梟， 狐狼野干及諸惡獸， 楂掣食噉骨肉狼籍， 風飃日曝雨漬霜封，
column2: “And perhaps your corpse might be exposed, and given over to the birds and beasts, so that all manner of evil beasts—crows and ravenous dogs, and carrion birds and owls, and foxes, wolves, and jackals— will rip it and tear it and eat and devour it, and the bones and flesh will litter the ground in a jumble, blasted by wind and baked by sun, drenched by rain and caked with frost, the limbs dismembered and flung apart, scattered separately here and there.

column1: 支節解散零落異所； 或有積薪以火焚葬， 筋骨焦爛血肉消化， 臭煙熢㶿四面充塞，
column2: “Or else it might be that a pyre is built, and you are cremated in the fire, and the muscles and bones are burnt to bits, and the blood and flesh steam off, and putrid smoke billows and reeks and chokes on all sides, and when the fire dies, the bones will have vanished, and flown in ash and scattered as dust.

column1: 火滅骨消灰飛塵散； 或有掘地埋殯墳陵， 經歷多時肉消骨腐。
column2: “Or it might be that a hole is dug in the ground, and you will be interred and encoffined in a burial mound, and after much time passes, the flesh will waste away and the bones will rot.

column1: 「大王當知！
column2: “O great king!

column1: 此身如是變壞無常， 一切眾生及以諸行皆悉如是， 非常非恒不可保信， 皆變易法迅速不停， 流轉移動終歸壞滅，
column2: Know that just as the body is thus mutable, destructible, and impermanent, all beings, and all compounded things, are without exception similarly impermanent, inconstant, and not to be trusted; they are all mutable things, which hurtle onward ceaselessly, churning and shifting, destined for ultimate destruction; from moment to moment they slip away and decay, and finally turn to ash; in the end, they are uniformly bound for the maw of annihilation; they are perishable things, beset with terrors, attended by sudden calamity, and they multiply our woes; they are all alike things that fall to ruin, and are broken and scattered.

column1: 念念遷謝後為灰燼， 究竟同趣滅盡之門， 是失壞法， 有諸怖畏有諸災橫多諸愁惱， 皆是墜墮零落斷壞離散之法。 「是故， 大王！
column2: “Thus, O great king!

column1: 應善勤修， 隨無常觀、隨盡滅觀， 勿為貪欲之所染污， 勿為瞋恚之所鼓動， 勿為愚癡之所覆蔽， 勿復耽染王富貴樂， 勿復耽染王自在樂， 勿復耽染王愛欲樂， 勿復耽染及餘所受諸欲樂具。
column2: You should properly and diligently practice the contemplation that follows impermanence (with each inbreath and outbreath), and the contemplation that follows cessation (with each inbreath and outbreath); be not polluted by the taint of greed; be not driven by the drumbeat of wrath; be not veiled by ignorance; wallow no more in the pleasures of wealth and rank of a king; wallow no more in the pleasures of power of a king; wallow no more in the pleasures of love and sensuality of a king; wallow no more in the other objects of desire and pleasure that you enjoy.

column1: 應當滅除財命憍逸， 應當驚懼無常死魔， 不與人期奄忽而至。
column2: You should root out and quash all arrogance and negligence with regard to wealth and life; you should ever fear the devil’s legions of impermanence and death, whose advent is sudden and unforeseen.

column1: 為大國主， 應以正法勿以非法， 應隨法行勿隨非法，
column2: “You reign as lord of a great state, and you should do so by means of righteous Dharma, and not by means of perversions of Dharma; you should conduct yourself in accordance with Dharma, and not in accordance with what is not Dharma.

column1: 應愍眾生皆如一子， 應當至誠護持佛法， 紹隆三寶勿復餘顧。
column2: You should feel tenderly for beings as if they were your only son; you should most sincerely protect and sustain the Buddha’s Dharma, and secure the succession of the Three Jewels; do not any longer have regard for other things.

column1: 所以者何？
column2: And why is that?

column1: 生死海中流轉無始， 唯佛正法是大津梁， 千萬億劫實難值故。
column2: Because we tumble and churn in the ocean of birth-and-death from beginningless time, and only the true Dharma of the Buddha is our bridge, but in a thousand, a myriad, a billion kalpas, it is truly difficult to meet with it.

column1: 「大王當知！
column2: “O great king!

column1: 我終不說獲得世間諸欲樂具， 積聚受用名富貴者， 我說獲得諸佛正法聖慧財寶積聚受用， 乃名圓滿真富貴者。
column2: Know that I have never taught that the winning of the objects of worldly desire and pleasure, accumulating them, and enjoying them is called wealth and rank; I teach that the winning of the wealth and treasure of the sagely wisdom of the true Dharma of the Buddhas, accumulating it, and enjoying it—only that is called perfect, true wealth and rank.

column1: 是故， 大王！
column2: For this reason, O great king!

column1: 應當厭離世間所有諸欲樂具， 應當願求諸佛正法聖慧財寶。 」時薄伽梵說是經已， 憍薩羅主勝軍大王，
column2: You should turn away in disgust from all objects of worldly desire and pleasure; you should seek the wealth and treasure of the sagely wisdom of the true Dharma of the Buddhas.” At that time, when the Bhagavat had preached this sutra, the Lord of Kośala, the great king Prasenajit, and the assembly of humans, gods, etc.

column1: 及諸世間天人等眾， 聞佛所說皆大歡喜， 信受奉行。
column2: of all the worlds, hearing what was preached by the Buddha, all greatly rejoiced, accepted it in faith, and reverentially upheld it.
